question_text: A 37-year-old man presents to the clinic because of painful, severe blistering over his buttocks for the past week. About a year ago, he noticed a similar outbreak on his inner thighs, but it receded within a few days on its own. Physical examination shows the blisters are tense, and rubbing the affected skin does not result in ‘popping’ of the blisters. A biopsy shows the entire epidermis lifting away from the basal lamina with extensive inflammatory infiltrates abundant with eosinophils. Immunofluorescence shows a linear pattern of immune complex deposits. Which of the following cellular structures, if defective, is most likely involved in the formation of these blisters?
